name: Signed-Facet Shell and Residual Core
statement: For a proper family $R\subsetneq Q_E$, let $\mathcal O(R)$ be the signed facets $F_{e,i}$ contained in $R$, let $F_R$ be the face opposite every member of $\mathcal O(R)$, and put $B_R=R\cap F_R$. At most one sign of each coordinate occurs in $\mathcal O(R)$, and $R=(Q_E\setminus F_R)\mathbin{\dot\cup}B_R$. After suppressing the coordinates fixed on $F_R$, $R$ is ample exactly when $B_R$ is ample, and $R$ is dismantlable ample exactly when $B_R$ is dismantlable ample. The residual core $B_R$ has no full signed facet in its residual cube; the empty core is allowed as a terminal row.
proof: A proper row cannot contain both facets of one coordinate. The union of all contained facets is exactly the complement of their common opposite face, and the remaining row points form $B_R$. After reorientation, if $K$ is the set of shell coordinates and $L$ the rest, then $R=((Q_K\setminus\{\mathbf1_K\})\times Q_L)\cup(\{\mathbf1_K\}\times B_R)$. Adding the coordinates of $K$ one at a time is an iterated peripheral expansion with one full-cube section, so the exact expansion criterion transfers both ampleness and peelability between $R$ and $B_R$. A full residual facet in $B_R$ would extend through the shell to a full facet of $R$, contradicting its omission from $\mathcal O(R)$.
comments: The regression certificate exhaustively checks all 65,808 proper rows in dimensions one through four, including the shell decomposition, both equivalences, and the empty-core corner and safe-deletion formulas.
